ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: Figure 1 is a line chart of the latitudinal position of the western Pacific subtropical high ridge line in July-August around 1955-1990, with the vertical axis being latitude, roughly from 24°N to 28°N. Observing near 1989 on the horizontal axis, the line is at a relatively low position, and the latitude of the subtropical high ridge line is approximately near 24°N to 25°N, obviously shifted southward. Then reason: the question stem states that China's frontal zone is approximately located 5° to 8° north of the subtropical high ridge line, therefore the frontal rain belt in July-August 1989 was approximately near 29°N to 33°N. The North China region is roughly located north of 35°N, lying north of this main rain belt and not within the main precipitation belt, so the precipitation in China's North China region in July-August 1989 should have been below normal.
